metadata.design_principle: Flat (dataset, language) rows — deduplicated across benchmarks.

benchmarks.brief_description: AfroBench is a comprehensive multi-task benchmark for evaluating LLM performance across 64 African languages, comprising 15 NLP tasks and 22 datasets spanning NLU, text generation, QA, and reasoning. It aggregates existing African language evaluation datasets and introduces one new dataset (AfriADR) for diacritics restoration.

A multilingual evaluation suite for assessing open-ended generation quality of LLMs, consisting of 25,750 prompts: 250 original human-curated prompts in each of 7 languages, 200 machine-translated prompts from English Dolly in 101 languages (114 dialects), and human post-edited translations of those prompts in 6 languages.

A fully parallel multiple-choice machine reading comprehension (MRC) benchmark spanning 122 language variants across 29 scripts and 27 language families, with 900 questions based on passages from the FLORES-200 dataset. Questions were created in English and professionally translated to all target languages.

A large-scale human evaluation benchmark for assessing cultural localisation in machine translation by multilingual LLMs. Evaluates 7 LLMs across 15 target languages with 5 native-speaker raters per language on both full-text translations and segment-level culturally nuanced language (idioms, puns, holidays, cultural concepts) on a 0-3 ordinal quality scale.

BenchMAX is a comprehensive multilingual evaluation suite covering 10 diverse tasks across 6 capabilities (instruction following, code generation, reasoning, long context understanding, tool use, and translation) in 17 languages. Data is machine-translated from English and post-edited by three native annotators per sample to ensure quality.

BHASA is a holistic linguistic and cultural evaluation suite for LLMs in Southeast Asian languages, comprising an NLP benchmark (8 tasks across NLU, NLG, NLR), LINDSEA (a handcrafted linguistic diagnostic toolkit covering syntax, semantics, and pragmatics), and cultural diagnostics (cultural representation and sensitivity). It currently covers Indonesian, Vietnamese, Thai, and Tamil for the NLP benchmark, and Indonesian and Tamil for LINDSEA and cultural diagnostics.

BhashaBench V1 is a domain-specific, multi-task, bilingual (English and Hindi) benchmark containing 74,166 question-answer pairs across four India-centric domains: Agriculture, Legal, Finance, and Ayurveda. Questions are sourced from authentic government and professional examination papers, spanning 90+ subdomains and 500+ topics.

benchmarks.brief_description: BoolQ is a reading comprehension dataset of 16,000 naturally occurring yes/no questions paired with Wikipedia passages. Questions are gathered from anonymized Google search queries and annotated by humans following the Natural Questions pipeline.

BUFFET (Benchmark of Unified Format Few-shot Transfer Evaluation) is a benchmark for few-shot cross-lingual transfer that unifies 15 diverse NLP tasks across 54 typologically diverse languages in a sequence-to-sequence format, providing fixed few-shot examples and instructions for rigorous comparisons of multilingual language models using both fine-tuning and in-context learning.

CL-IFEval and CL-GSM Symbolic are cross-lingual functional evaluation benchmarks created by translating English IFEval (541 prompts) and GSM-Symbolic (100 templates) into French, Spanish, Hindi, Arabic, and Yoruba via Google Translate with native-speaker validation, designed to measure functional multilingual performance and robustness of LLMs beyond static data benchmarks.

CulturalBench is an English-only benchmark of 1,696 human-written and human-verified multiple-choice questions assessing LMs' cultural knowledge across 45 global regions and 17 cultural topics. It includes two evaluation setups: CulturalBench-Easy (multiple-choice) and CulturalBench-Hard (True/False binary for each option, yielding 6,784 questions).

datasets.task_type: cultural knowledge QA (multiple-choice and binary True/False)

benchmarks.brief_description: A high-quality evaluation benchmark for multilingual machine translation consisting of 3001 English Wikipedia sentences professionally translated into 101 languages, enabling many-to-many evaluation of 10,100 translation directions.

FLUID QA is the first multilingual benchmark evaluating figurative language usage in dialogue across English, Korean, and Chinese, covering four rhetorical categories (idiom, metaphor, simile, sarcasm). It is accompanied by FLUTE-bi, a sentence-level binary classification diagnostic task for figurative recognition.

datasets.task_type: multiple-choice QA (cloze-style figurative expression selection in multi-turn dialogue)
binary classification (figurative vs. literal sentence-level recognition)

benchmarks.brief_description: GSM8K is a dataset of 8.5K high-quality grade school math word problems in English with natural language solutions, requiring 2-8 step reasoning using basic arithmetic operations. It was designed to diagnose multi-step mathematical reasoning failures in large language models.

IberoBench is a multilingual, multi-task benchmark for evaluating LLMs in five Iberian languages (Catalan, European Spanish, Basque, Galician, and European Portuguese), consisting of 62 tasks divided into 179 subtasks across 10 categories, built on the LM Evaluation Harness framework. It combines 40 existing high-quality datasets with 22 newly created or translated datasets, emphasizing quality, reproducibility, and cultural adaptation.

A human-curated parallel corpus of 13,000 sentence pairs spanning 11 Indian dialects and 2 standard languages (Hindi and Odia) from three Indian states (Himachal Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh, Odisha), used to construct a multi-task benchmark evaluating dialect classification, multiple-choice question answering, and machine translation between dialects and their corresponding standard languages.

IndicIFEval is a benchmark for evaluating verifiable instruction-following in 14 Indic languages, comprising two subsets: IndicIFEval-Trans (translated and localized from English IFEval) and IndicIFEval-Ground (synthetically generated instructions grounded in native Indic content from the Sangraha corpus), with ~800 human-verified examples per language.

IndicMMLU-Pro is a machine-translated adaptation of the English MMLU-Pro benchmark into 9 Indic languages (Hindi, Bengali, Telugu, Marathi, Tamil, Gujarati, Urdu, Kannada, Punjabi), covering 14 subject categories for evaluating LLM multi-task language understanding. Translation was performed using IndicTrans2 and validated via back-translation metrics and expert proofreading by 13 native-speaker reviewers.

IndicNLG Benchmark is a collection of datasets for benchmarking NLG performance across 5 diverse tasks (biography generation, headline generation, sentence summarization, paraphrase generation, question generation) spanning 11 Indic languages, comprising approximately 8.5M examples total. It is the first NLG benchmark for Indic languages.

IndicNLPSuite provides monolingual corpora (IndicCorp), pre-trained word embeddings (IndicFT), language models (IndicBERT), and an NLU evaluation benchmark (IndicGLUE) for 11 major Indian languages from the Indo-Aryan and Dravidian families, comprising newly created semi-automatic datasets and curated existing datasets across tasks including text classification, QA, NER, NLI, paraphrase detection, and sentiment analysis.

A human-curated benchmark of over 13,000 multiple-choice questions covering 11 low- and extremely low-resource Indic languages, sourced from UGC-NET graduate-level examinations administered by the Government of India. Questions are classified as language understanding or general knowledge, and annotated with six question types (MCQ, assertion & reason, list matching, fill in the blanks, identify incorrect statement, ordering).

IndicXTREME is a human-supervised NLU benchmark for Indic languages consisting of nine diverse tasks (five classification, two structure prediction, one QA, one retrieval) covering 20 languages from 4 language families, with 105 evaluation sets of which 52 are new contributions. It is designed to test zero-shot cross-lingual transfer of pretrained language models.

IndiSentiment140 is a sentiment analysis dataset for 22 Indian languages created by machine-translating the English Sentiment140 Twitter corpus (1.6M tweets) into each language using Google Translate, preserving the original binary sentiment labels (positive/negative).

IrokoBench is a human-translated benchmark for 17 typologically-diverse low-resource African languages, comprising three tasks: natural language inference (AfriXNLI, from XNLI), multi-choice knowledge QA (AfriMMLU, from MMLU), and mathematical reasoning (AfriMGSM, from MGSM). It evaluates LLMs on complex reasoning and knowledge-intensive tasks for African languages.

JailNewsBench is the first benchmark for evaluating LLM robustness against jailbreak-induced fake news generation, spanning 34 regions and 22 languages with approximately 300k instances, 8 evaluation sub-metrics through LLM-as-a-Judge, and 5 jailbreak attack methods.

A comprehensive multilingual safety benchmark for LLMs comprising 45k entries across 12 languages (high-, medium-, and low-resource), curated using a combination of translated, transcreated, and natively-sourced data. Features a hierarchical safety taxonomy with 5 domains and 23 subtypes, severity-level annotations (L0-L3), and both direct (MCQ) and indirect evaluation frameworks including oversensitivity assessment.

M-IFEval is a multilingual extension of the IFEval benchmark that evaluates LLM instruction-following abilities in French, Japanese, and Spanish (plus English from the original IFEval), using both shared and language-specific verifiable instructions covering formatting, punctuation, script-based, and special-character constraints.

M3Exam is a benchmark of 12,317 multiple-choice questions sourced from real official human exams in 9 languages across 3 educational levels (primary, middle, high school), covering 4 subject categories (language, math, social science, natural science), with approximately 23% of questions requiring image processing.

MAKIEVAL is an automatic multilingual framework for evaluating cultural awareness in LLMs through open-ended text generation, leveraging Wikidata as a cross-lingual anchor to extract and link cultural entities without translation. It evaluates 7 LLMs across 13 languages, 19 countries/regions, and 6 culturally salient topics using four metrics: granularity, diversity, culture specificity, and culture consensus.

datasets.task_type: open-ended text generation for cultural awareness evaluation

benchmarks.brief_description: MATH is a dataset of 12,500 challenging competition mathematics problems (from AMC 10, AMC 12, AIME, etc.) with step-by-step solutions in LaTeX, spanning 7 subjects and 5 difficulty levels. It is accompanied by AMPS, a large auxiliary pretraining corpus of over 5 million mathematics problems from Khan Academy and Mathematica scripts.

MaXIFE is a multilingual and cross-lingual instruction-following evaluation benchmark covering 23 languages with 1667 verifiable instruction tasks across 47 instruction subcategories, combining rule-based and model-based evaluation strategies.

MEGA (Multilingual Evaluation of Generative AI) is the first large-scale benchmarking of generative LLMs across multilingual settings, evaluating GPT-3.5, GPT-4, and BLOOMZ on 16 existing NLP datasets spanning 70 typologically diverse languages covering 21 language families, with analysis of prompting strategies, performance disparities across languages, and test data contamination.

MILU (Multi-task Indic Language Understanding Benchmark) is a comprehensive evaluation benchmark covering 8 domains and 41 subjects across 11 Indic languages (including English), with ~79,617 multiple-choice questions sourced from Indian national, state, and regional competitive examinations. It emphasizes India-centric, culturally relevant knowledge alongside standard academic subjects.

MMLU-ProX is a multilingual benchmark extending MMLU-Pro to 29 typologically diverse languages, containing 11,829 parallel multiple-choice questions (10 options) per language across 57 subjects and 14 disciplines. It uses a semi-automated LLM translation pipeline with expert verification to enable direct cross-linguistic comparison of LLM reasoning capabilities.

datasets.task_type: multiple-choice QA (10 options) with chain-of-thought reasoning

benchmarks.brief_description: MMTEB (Massive Multilingual Text Embedding Benchmark) is a large-scale, community-driven expansion of MTEB, covering over 500 quality-controlled evaluation tasks across 10 task categories and 1051 languages (250+ excluding bitext mining), spanning diverse domains including fiction, social media, medical texts, and programming documentation. It constructs several sub-benchmarks including MTEB(Multilingual) with 132 tasks, MTEB(Europe) with 74 tasks, MTEB(Indic) with 23 tasks, and MTEB(eng, v2) with 41 tasks.

MUCH is a multilingual claim-level hallucination benchmark comprising 4,873 LLM-generated responses (20,751 claims) across four European languages (English, French, Spanish, German), with binary factuality annotations and 24 logits per token, designed for evaluating uncertainty quantification methods under realistic deployment conditions.

MUG-Eval is a language-agnostic proxy evaluation framework that assesses LLMs' multilingual generation capabilities by transforming existing benchmarks into conversational information-gap tasks, using task success rate as a proxy for generation quality. It evaluates 8 LLMs across 30 languages (high/mid/low-resource) on three tasks without requiring language-specific NLP tools, human annotations, or LLM-as-judge, and claims scalability to 2,102 languages via GlotLID.

A multilingual jailbreak dataset comprising 3150 samples across 10 languages (English plus 9 non-English), designed to evaluate LLM safety under two scenarios: unintentional (non-English users inadvertently bypassing safety) and intentional (malicious users combining multilingual prompts with jailbreak instructions).

Naamapadam is the largest publicly available NER dataset for 11 major Indian languages from two language families (Indo-Aryan and Dravidian), containing 5.7M sentences and 9.4M entities across three categories (Person, Location, Organization). Training data is automatically created via annotation projection from English using parallel corpora, while manually annotated test sets are provided for 9 languages.

A large-scale multilingual benchmark of 425K naturally occurring prompts across 17 languages for evaluating neural toxic degeneration in LLMs, created by scraping over 100M web-text documents from mC4 and The Pile corpora and scoring them with Perspective API. PTPSmall is a stratified 5K-per-language subset for lower-cost benchmarking.

SEA-HELM (SouthEast Asian Holistic Evaluation of Language Models) is a holistic multilingual and multicultural LLM evaluation suite for Southeast Asian languages, comprising five core pillars: NLP Classics, LLM-Specifics, SEA Linguistics, SEA Culture, and Safety. It currently supports Filipino, Indonesian, Tamil, Thai, and Vietnamese, combining collated native-language and translated datasets with newly created benchmarks (SEA-IFEval, SEA-MTBench, LINDSEA).

TriviaQA is a large-scale reading comprehension dataset containing over 650K question-answer-evidence triples, with 95K question-answer pairs authored by trivia enthusiasts and independently gathered evidence documents from Wikipedia and the Web. It tests complex compositional questions, lexical/syntactic variability, and multi-sentence reasoning.

A comprehensive, natively developed multilingual language understanding benchmark for Turkic languages, consisting of 38,139 middle- and high-school level multiple-choice questions across 11 academic subjects in 9 Turkic languages (Azerbaijani, Crimean Tatar, Karakalpak, Kazakh, Kyrgyz, Tatar, Turkish, Uyghur, and Uzbek). TUMLU-mini is a balanced and manually verified subset with ~100 questions per subject per language.

Uhura is a benchmark for evaluating scientific question answering and truthfulness in six low-resource African languages (Amharic, Hausa, Northern Sotho, Swahili, Yoruba, Zulu), created via professional human translation of ARC-Easy and TruthfulQA from English.

XGLUE is a cross-lingual benchmark covering 11 tasks (both understanding and generation) across 19 languages, with English-only training data for each task. It includes 5 existing multilingual datasets and 6 new tasks from Search, Ads, and News scenarios.

XNLI is a cross-lingual natural language inference evaluation corpus consisting of 7500 human-annotated development and test examples translated from English MultiNLI data into 14 other languages (15 total), covering three-way NLI classification (entailment, contradiction, neutral).

datasets.task_type: Natural Language Inference (3-way classification: entailment, contradiction, neutral)

benchmarks.brief_description: XOR QA is a cross-lingual open-retrieval question answering benchmark built on 40K information-seeking questions across 7 typologically diverse non-English languages (inherited from TyDi QA's unanswerable questions). It defines three tasks of increasing complexity: XOR-Retrieve (cross-lingual paragraph retrieval), XOR-EnglishSpan (L-to-English open-retrieval QA), and XOR-Full (round-trip answer generation in the target language).

XQuAD is a cross-lingual extractive question answering benchmark consisting of 240 paragraphs and 1190 question-answer pairs from the SQuAD v1.1 development set, professionally translated from English into 10 languages (Spanish, German, Greek, Russian, Turkish, Arabic, Vietnamese, Thai, Chinese, Hindi).

XTREME (Cross-lingual TRansfer Evaluation of Multilingual Encoders) is a multi-task benchmark for evaluating the cross-lingual generalization capabilities of multilingual representations. It covers 40 typologically diverse languages spanning 12 language families and includes 9 tasks across classification, structured prediction, question answering, and sentence retrieval.

XTREME-R (XTREME Revisited) is a multilingual benchmark consisting of 10 natural language understanding tasks covering 50 typologically diverse languages, extending XTREME with more challenging tasks including language-agnostic retrieval, a multilingual diagnostic suite (MultiCheckList), and fine-grained evaluation capabilities via an interactive leaderboard.

XTREME-UP is a multilingual benchmark focusing on user-centric tasks in a scarce-data setting for 88 under-represented languages across 9 key technologies including ASR, OCR, MT, and information access tasks. It standardizes multilingual in-language fine-tuning based on realistic annotation costs (8 hours per language).
